# Success
<!--
Projects should have a definition of done that is measurable, and a
thorough understanding going in of what the risks are to delivery
-->

## Definition of done
<!--
What does success look like?
-->
The project will be complete when a publicly available, installable **fedvalidateR** package provides the specified local-validation and central-synthesis workflows, documented study and site-results structures, automated tests, tutorials, synthetic multisite examples and an end-to-end public-data demonstration. Additional testing in Brazilian intensive care or ISARIC settings will be subject to relevant approvals and is not required for core project completion.

## Measuring success
<!--
How will we know when success is achieved, what markers can we use
along the way
-->
Success will be assessed by:

- passing R package checks and all critical automated tests;
- agreement with independent reference calculations within prespecified tolerances;
- successful end-to-end analysis of at least three contrasting synthetic sites;
- at least **80% test coverage** for core functions;
- reproducible tutorials and demonstration materials;
- structured feedback from at least **five intended users**, with critical issues resolved; and
- public release of the package, code and documentation.

## Future work
<!--
How could this be extended / developed in the future by yourself
and/or the community in general?
-->
Future releases may extend **fedvalidateR** to other outcome types, model recalibration, decision-curve analysis, additional disclosure controls and DataSHIELD integration. Further development may also include multilingual documentation and CRAN submission, guided by user and community feedback.
